kind: offline actual CPU-skinned geometry visual spot-check
reviewed: Every rendered 24Hz frame inspected in chronological image sheets, all 27 larger keyframe images represented in sheets, and 12 full-resolution three-quarter closeups inspected. Videos encoded at normal speed and ffprobe verified; no claim of real-time browser playback.
camera: Full sequences: fixed one-view camera from unchanged renderer, world translation preserved. Static closeups: centered rigid display transform with 45-degree yaw, labeled separately; two contact camera bounds include the sphere to prevent cropping.
findings: The mirrored low-wide catches remain left/right counterparts through transfer, chest hold, leg tuck, rise, and final standing hold.

The sphere remains visibly associated with the catching/gathering hands through the reviewed sequence; no gross detachment or teleport is visible. Early transfer uses an open palm/edge contact and the other hand approaches.
Front and three-quarter views show the forearms routing around the held sphere. No gross sphere-through-forearm or sphere-through-torso event is visible at the rendered resolution.

The low-wide motions descend from an aerial catch, fold legs toward support, and lift into a planted standing hold. The central catch rises from its low squat. No gross shoe/limb breach of the rendered floor is visible.
Final standing hold remains stable through the last sample at +2.833333s.
residualStylization: Sharp elbow and wrist folds remain visible, especially during +0.167s transfer and the side-lying tuck.
Fingers remain quite open and do not wrap the ball like a detailed closed grasp; from oblique angles some contact is an edge or is occluded.
Knees compress into angular folds; the side-lying pose and toe/edge-supported rise still look stylized rather than fully natural biomechanics.
Low-sample simplified CPU materials show noise and seam/crease artifacts. These images do not test textures or browser shader appearance.
limits: Three selected fresh catches are visual spot checks, not exhaustive fixture coverage.
No WebGL, GPU, browser texture, or real-device performance validation.
Image review cannot certify sub-pixel triangle clearance; quantitative gates remain separate.
